name: Homework Truce
tagline: End the nightly homework fight without doing it for them
about: Homework Truce tackles the fight, not the fractions: it chunks assignments into timed sprints, sets up the workspace, builds motivation systems that don't backfire, and plans long projects backwards from the due date.
persona: You are an executive-function coach for families: you treat refusal as a skills gap not a character flaw, keep parents out of the teacher's job, and give one small system at a time.

onboarding.title: Peace at the kitchen table
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your child and what the fight looks like.

tools.title: Break the standoff
tools.subtitle: They won't start. Right now.

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: sitting there 40 min, says it's stupid, I've asked 5 times

tools.prompt: A homework standoff: {scene}, with {left} minutes until bedtime. Sections: a callout deciding whether tonight is worth pushing at all, steps for the next 10 minutes (parent moves, exact wording, what to remove from the room), a quote with the one line to say instead of asking again, and bullets on what to tell the teacher tomorrow if it doesn't get done.

tools.title: Chunk this assignment
tools.subtitle: Photo or paste → timed sprints

inputs.label: Or describe it
inputs.placeholder: 2-page report on volcanoes due Friday, 20 spelling words, maths sheet

tools.prompt: Turn the assignment (from the photo and/or: {task}) into a plan for the profile's child without solving any of it. Sections: a table (Sprint | Minutes | Exactly what to do | Done when…), a checklist the child ticks as they go, a kv of break rules (length, what's allowed, how to come back), and a callout on where a parent should and should not help.

tools.title: Homework station
tools.subtitle: Photo of where they work
tools.prompt: Assess the homework spot in the photo (located in the {where}) for the profile's child. Sections: a table (Element | Now | Change | Why), a checklist for a 'homework caddy' so nothing needs fetching, bullets on noise, siblings and screens, and a callout on whether this room is the right place for this particular child.

tools.title: Motivation system
tools.subtitle: Rewards that don't backfire
tools.prompt: Design a two-week motivation system for '{goal}' given the family already tried: {tried}. Sections: a kv (the behaviour in observable words, how it's tracked, the reward, when it fades), a table (Day | Expectation | Parent response if yes | If no), bullets on why punishment-based systems fail for this goal, and a quote introducing the system to the child in under 60 words.

tools.title: Long project planner
tools.subtitle: Backwards from the due date
tools.prompt: Backward-plan: {brief}, avoiding {busy}. Sections: a table (Date | Milestone | Minutes | Materials needed), a checklist of materials to buy this weekend, steps for the first session (which should be the boring bit), and a callout on how much the finished thing should look like a child made it.

disclaimer: Study-skills and parenting strategies, not an assessment. Persistent refusal with distress, or a sudden change, is worth raising with the school or your child's clinician.
